title: Aegis Health - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Aegis Health's private deployment requirements: VPC networking, peering constraints, private endpoints, region availability, and encryption/KMS controls. Redwood AE + SE outlined Private offering, network patterns (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), IP range needs, and security attestations. Customer asked about region restrictions, cross-account peering, and audit log retention. Next steps: send security pack, network diagram and IP ranges, schedule technical deep dive with networking team.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-12 15:00 PT | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Maya Turner (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Aegis CTO), Priya Nair (SecOps), Daniel Reyes (SRE)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, I'm the account lead here at Redwood Inference. Samir, our solutions engineer, is with me. Quick intro?
[00:08] Jordan (Aegis - CTO): Jordan here, CTO at Aegis. We've got Priya on SecOps and Daniel from SRE. We're evaluating private deployments for PHI workloads.
[00:16] Maya: Great, thanks. Goal for today is to understand your networking constraints, region needs, and security requirements so we can map Redwood Private or Dedicated options - specifically VPC peering vs private endpoints.
[00:24] Samir (Redwood SE): Quick note, sometimes in our docs we say "Redwood Dedicate" - that's a typo you'll see occasionally, sorry - but the capabilities differ: Private gives you a customer control plane and VPC integration.
[00:35] Priya (SecOps): Primary ask: we need assurance on no egress to public internet for model inference and encryption keys managed by our KMS/HSM. Also audit logs and retention for six months.
[00:44] Daniel (SRE): And network-wise we have strict CIDR allocations and no overlapping ranges with partner networks. Peering has to be cross-account in our AWS org.
[00:52] Maya: Understood. Samir, can you walk through the common network patterns we support?
[00:56] Samir: Sure. We typically support three patterns: VPC peering (classic, low-latency), AWS PrivateLink / Interface endpoints, and a customer-managed Transit Gateway approach for complex routing. Peering is simplest but doesn't work across regions, PrivateLink works cross-account and provides private endpoints without peering, but has ENI requirements and estimated IP consumption. For on-prem we do IPSEC VPN or Direct Connect into a VPC.
[01:20] Jordan: So peering doesn't cross regions - if we need a multi-region DR what do you recommend?
[01:24] Samir: Usually we recommend deploying Redwood Private in the target region and using a multi-region routing policy. We can replicate model versions; fallback can be configured. If you need single-VPC multi-region, that's not supported with peering alone. PrivateLink across regions is also limited, so we often use region-specific Private deployments.
[01:39] Priya: For encryption - can keys be in our KMS or do you require Redwood-managed keys?
[01:44] Maya: You can bring your own keys (BYOK) via customer-managed KMS. For HSM-level controls we have integrations; Samir can share the KMS flow.
[01:51] Samir: Right - we support envelope encryption with customer KMS. For HSM-backed keys we integrate with customer's HSM or use cloud provider HSM via CMKs; we store minimal metadata and do not persist cleartext model inputs in logs unless you opt in.
[02:05] Jordan: What about audit logs and SAML/SSO?
[02:08] Maya: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and provide audit logs with configurable retention. SOC2 and ISO artifacts are in the security pack we'll send. Retention policies are adjustable if you have a legal requirement.
[02:19] Daniel: Network team will want exact IP ranges and egress ports. Any idea of port ranges?
[02:23] Samir: Typical egress is TCP:443 for control plane, and we use additional ranges for inter-node traffic depending on deployment size - we'll include a table in the network doc. Also note for PrivateLink we allocate ENIs in your subnets, so you need available IPs.
[02:36] Priya: That ENI consumption is important for us, we run tight subnets.
[02:39] Samir: Understood - we'll include expected IP counts per node and suggestions for subnet sizing.
[02:44] Jordan: Are there bandwidth/cost implications if we replicate models across regions?
[02:48] Samir: Yes, there's storage and sync cost. For large models we recommend either pulling artifacts on demand or using a shared S3 bucket with replication; cost varies. We'll outline best practices.
[02:58] Maya: Quick qualification: are you looking for a fully managed private control plane or just dedicated capacity in our hosted environment?
[03:04] Jordan: For compliance we prefer a private control plane or on-prem package. Hosted is fine for dev. Production needs to be private.
[03:10] Maya: Good, that helps. Timeline and success criteria?
[03:14] Jordan: Timeline is Q4 pilot, production in Q1. Success is <120ms 95th perc latency for our customer-facing assistants, and SOC2-ready controls. Cost target is within 20% of current managed infra spend - but quality is priority.
[03:30] Samir: The latency target is doable depending on region and instance types. We'll recommend GPU instance classes and co-located region. Also batching settings impact latency; we can tune.
[03:40] Priya: Are you able to support private Egress-only NAT or must egress go through your infra?
[03:45] Maya: Egress can be routed through your VPC - we support VPC peering and private endpoints; you can control egress. For audit and DLP you might route through your proxies.
[03:55] Daniel: Any support for VPC peering across accounts inside our org?
[03:58] Samir: Yes, cross-account peering is supported. We'll need the peer owner IDs and route table updates. For complex topologies we recommend Transit Gateway.
[04:06] Jordan: You mentioned PrivateLink earlier - are there additional quotas or limits?
[04:09] Samir: AWS has ENI quotas per AZ; we'll provide guidance. Also each PrivateLink endpoint can consume several ENIs depending on scale. There's a per-region limit to be aware of.
[04:20] Maya: Just to flag, customers sometimes compare us to Anthropic or SageMaker for managed endpoints - any concerns?
[04:26] Jordan: It's mostly cost and proven performance; we have internal proof points with Anthropic but are open. We want to see measured latencies in our region.
[04:33] Maya: We can run a pilot with a benchmark harness. Samir, we'll include a benchmarking plan.
[04:37] Samir: Yep - small-scale perf benchmark, synthetic traffic from your VPC to validate 95th percentiles. We'll also show KV cache effects and batching tradeoffs.
[04:47] Priya: About data residency: are all logs and data kept in the chosen region?
[04:51] Samir: Yes - when you deploy in a region, logs and storage are kept in that region by default unless you opt for cross-region replication. We'll document retention and movement.
[04:58] Jordan: For keys, if we use our KMS in us-west-2, can we still deploy in eu-west-1?
[05:03] Samir: Cross-region KMS usage has added latency and constraints. Generally we recommend co-locating KMS with the region to avoid cross-region key grants, or replicate keys via provider mechanisms.
[05:13] Daniel: Any special networking for model updates and image pulls?
[05:17] Samir: Engine pulls images from a secure artifact store; we can either pull over private connectivity (S3 VPC endpoints) or allow pre-warmed images in your VPC. We'll include options.
[05:27] Priya: Our legal team will want to see the data flows diagram - can you provide that?
[05:30] Maya: Yes, that's part of the pack. We'll include a data flow diagram, network diagram, and sample ACLs.
[05:36] Jordan: On billing - do you have reserved capacity for Dedicated?
[05:40] Maya: Yes, Dedicated and Reserved capacity are options. Private is typically contracted with a platform fee plus capacity commit. We'll send pricing tiers.
[05:47] Priya: Any certifications beyond SOC2?
[05:50] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts; FedRAMP is on roadmap but not out of the box. We'll mark items that impact FedRAMP for your compliance team.
[05:57] Daniel: Last question - do you support IP allow lists and strict egress filtering?
[06:01] Samir: Yes, you can restrict egress to specific IP ranges, and we publish our outbound IPs. For PrivateLink, connections are inside your VPC so allow lists are simpler.
[06:10] Jordan: Okay, sounds good. What's the immediate next step?
[06:13] Maya: We'll follow up with the security pack and network doc today/tomorrow, and set a technical deep dive. Anything else?
[06:19] Priya: Please include ENI counts and expected ephemeral port ranges.
[06:23] Samir: Will do.
[06:25] Maya: Great. Recap of action items: Maya will send security and pricing docs; Samir will prepare network diagram and terraform sample; Jordan to share VPC CIDRs. We'll schedule the deep dive. Thanks all.

AUTO-GENERATED SUMMARY (optional): Discussion confirmed Aegis wants Private deployment for production due to PHI; key concerns around VPC peering, PrivateLink, ENI consumption, KMS BYOK, audit logs, and region-local deployments. Redwood to provide security pack, network diagram, and benchmark plan.

Action items (captured):
- Maya Turner: Send security pack (SOC2/ISO), pricing tiers, and next steps (by 2026-08-13).
- Samir Patel: Draft network diagram, ENI/IP estimates, and sample terraform for Private deployment (by 2026-08-14).

End of transcript.
